content.text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole (isatin 3-hydrazone).

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries HO2C at the meta position relative to the biaryl bond. The second ring has the biaryl bond at one carbon, OH on the adjacent carbon, and the HN–N= group on the next carbon after that. So the pattern is 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl on the second ring.

**Oxindole part.** C3 is double-bonded to N (the hydrazone), C2 is C=O, and N1 carries the 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. On the fused benzene ring, CN sits at position 6, which is para to C3a and meta to C7a. Checking the drawing: C3a is the ring-fusion carbon attached to C3, and C7a is attached to N. Going around from C3a, the ring runs C4 (top), C5 (right), C6 (bottom right, bearing CN), C7, then C7a. This matches CN at C6.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(C)c4)c5cc(C#N)ccc35)c2O
- Second ring: c2 is attached to the first ring, then cccc(N...)c2O. The ring atoms in order are C(biaryl), CH, CH, CH, C(N), C(OH). The C(OH) sits between C(N) and C(biaryl), which is correct.
- Oxindole: N1 is attached to c5, which is C7a. Then c is C7, c(C#N) is C6, c is C5, c is C4, and c35 is C3a, which closes to C3 and to the ring-fusion atom C7a. This is consistent.
- Aryl substituent: the 3,4-dimethylphenyl is written c4ccc(C)c(C)c4, with the attachment carbon first, then CH, CH, C(Me) at position 4, C(Me) at position 3, and CH. This is correct.

The hydrazone C=N geometry is not specified in the drawing in a way I can reliably assign, so I left it without stereo marks.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(C)c4)c5cc(C#N)ccc35)c2O
